title: Ovulation Calculation Methodology
overview: Ovulation calculators estimate the fertile window based on menstrual cycle patterns. While useful for family planning, they are not reliable for contraception due to natural cycle variability.

methods.name: Calendar Method (Rhythm Method)
methods.description: The standard calculation assumes ovulation occurs 14 days before the next expected period. The fertile window spans 5 days before ovulation through 1 day after.

formula.name: Standard Calendar Calculation
formula.expression:
Ovulation Day = Cycle Start + (Cycle Length - 14)
Fertile Window = Ovulation Day - 5 to Ovulation Day + 1

variables.meaning: Days from first day of period to next period

limitations: Does not account for cycle variability

methods.name: Variable Luteal Phase Method
methods.description: Accounts for the fact that luteal phase can vary between 10-16 days, creating a wider potential ovulation window.

formula.name: Variable Calculation
formula.expression:
Earliest Ovulation = Cycle Length - 16
Latest Ovulation = Cycle Length - 10
Extended Fertile Window = Earliest - 5 to Latest + 1
formula.description: Creates wider window for more conservative estimate

methods.accuracy: More conservative but captures actual ovulation better

methods.name: Symptothermal Method (Reference)
methods.description: Combines calendar calculation with basal body temperature (BBT) and cervical mucus observations for higher accuracy.

formula.name: Multi-Factor Method
formula.expression: Calendar baseline + BBT shift confirmation + Cervical mucus changes
formula.description: Temperature rises 0.3-0.6°C after ovulation; mucus becomes clear and stretchy at peak fertility

sources.name: ACOG - American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
Wilcox et al. - Timing of Intercourse and Fertility
Stanford et al. - Cervical Mucus Patterns

footnotes: Sperm can survive up to 5 days in the reproductive tract
The egg is viable for only 12-24 hours after ovulation
Cycle length can vary month to month even in 'regular' cycles
For accurate tracking, consider BBT, OPK tests, or cervical mucus monitoring
disclaimer: This calculator provides estimates only and should NOT be used as a contraceptive method. It is not accurate enough to prevent pregnancy. For family planning, consult a healthcare provider.
